name: Anima Anandkumar
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; B.S. IIT Madras 2004 and Ph.D. Cornell 2009 are documented, but without birth year age at those events cannot be verified, so a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established.
early_history_summary: Born in Mysore, India, to engineer parents; studied electrical engineering at IIT Madras (graduated 2004), then earned a Ph.D. at Cornell under Lang Tong (2009). Later held roles at UC Irvine, Amazon AWS, NVIDIA, and Caltech as Bren Professor of Computing.
family_context_summary: Parents are both engineers; grandfather was a mathematician; great-great-grandfather was Sanskrit scholar R. Shamasastry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents engineers; father mechanical engineer (IIT Madras) and mother electronics engineer per secondary profiles.
evidence_summary: Strong later-career ML research record (tensors, neural operators, NVIDIA/Caltech leadership) is well documented, but Wikipedia lists year of birth as missing and no reliable dated birth year was found. Without age verification, early eligibility cannot be coded.

name: Michael Birck
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1938; BSEE Purdue 1960 (age ~22) and MSEE NYU 1962 (age ~24) were ordinary educational milestones. Material founding of Tellabs occurred in 1975 at age ~37; no material company-founding or industry breakthrough by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born January 25, 1938, in Missoula, Montana; raised in Clinton, Indiana. Earned BSEE at Purdue (1960) and MSEE at NYU (1962), then worked at Bell Labs and Continental Telephone Labs before becoming director of engineering at Wescom (1968–1975).
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Midwestern upbringing in Indiana after birth in Montana.
evidence_summary: Birck's fame rests on co-founding Tellabs in 1975 and long CEO/chairman tenure. By age 26 he was a working engineer (Bell Labs / early career), not a founder of note. Died 2015 at age 77.

name: Franck Cappello
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found in reviewed sources. Ph.D. University of Paris XI in 1994 and later CNRS/INRIA/Argonne career are documented, but without birth year a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established.
early_history_summary: French computer scientist who received a Ph.D. from University of Paris XI in 1994, joined CNRS, later INRIA (Grid'5000 director 2003–2008), and Argonne National Laboratory as senior computer scientist leading resilience and scientific data compression work.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia notes year of birth missing. Career achievements (IEEE Fellow, Charles Babbage Award, ECP projects) are late-career recognitions. Eligibility requires dated age ≤26 milestone, which cannot be verified.

name: Nikita Bier
category: Consumer social app founder / product growth
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reliable dual sources. Co-founded tbh (launched 2017; acquired by Facebook Oct 2017) and later Gas (2022); secondary summaries estimate birth ~1991, which would place tbh near age 26, but birth year is not independently confirmed, so eligibility cannot be established under the strict age rule.
early_history_summary: UC Berkeley alumnus who built student product Politify around 2012, then iterated many consumer app pivots before tbh went viral among teens in 2017 and sold to Meta. Later co-founded Gas (acquired by Discord) and became Head of Product at X in 2025.
family_context_summary: Secondary sources describe a Ukrainian family background and speaking Russian at home; not strongly dual-sourced.
evidence_summary: tbh and Gas outcomes are material and well reported, but Wikipedia and mainstream profiles omit a precise birth year. Conservative coding requires confirmed age ≤26 at a dated milestone; estimated ~1991 birth is insufficient alone.

name: Jeff Hawkins
category: Palm Computing founder / mobile computing inventor
milestone_by_age_26: Born June 1, 1957; Cornell B.S. electrical engineering 1979 (age ~22). Joined GRiD Systems 1982 (age ~25) as software developer; GridPad and Palm founding came later (VP research late 1980s; Palm founded 1992 at age ~35). No material independent founding/product breakthrough by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Huntington, New York. Studied EE at Cornell (1979), joined GRiD Systems developing RAD software and later pen computing, then founded Palm Computing in 1992 and co-created the PalmPilot; later Handspring, Redwood Neuroscience Institute, and Numenta.
family_context_summary: Secondary sources note a father who was a natural tinkerer and boating enthusiast; limited documentation.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond informal tinkering culture.
evidence_summary: Palm/PalmPilot fame arrived in the mid-1990s when Hawkins was in his mid-to-late 30s. Early GRiD employment by 26 is ordinary industry work, not a material breakthrough under the rubric.

name: Chris Lattner
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and began implementing LLVM with Vikram Adve after joining UIUC in late 2000 (~age 22); completed the LLVM multi-stage optimization M.S. thesis in December 2002 at age ~24, establishing the compiler infrastructure that later became industry-standard.
early_history_summary: Started programming in high school (BASIC, then assembly/C/C++). Earned a B.S. in computer science at University of Portland (2000) while doing OS work on Sequent DYNIX/ptx. At UIUC he and Adve designed LLVM as research infrastructure; Ph.D. followed in 2005, then Apple hired him to productionize LLVM.
primary_early_advantage_tags: UIUC research lab, Vikram Adve mentorship, early systems programming reps
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Lattner's resume/LLVM publications align: birth 1978, BS 2000, LLVM design from late 2000, MS thesis Dec 2002. Second source: LLVM.org thesis page and ACM award narratives credit Lattner as principal designer. Family background not documented; scores conservative. Later created Clang, Swift, MLIR, and co-founded Modular (Mojo).
starting_point: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond U.S. education path (University of Portland undergrad; UIUC graduate research).
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Modular AI (Mojo language and AI developer platform); creator of LLVM, Clang, Swift, and MLIR; Modular reported acquisition agreement with Qualcomm in 2026.

trajectory.event: Joined UIUC as research assistant and began designing/implementing LLVM with Vikram Adve after BS from University of Portland.
Completed M.S. thesis 'LLVM: An Infrastructure for Multi-Stage Optimization,' establishing the core LLVM design.
Completed Ph.D. at UIUC and was hired by Apple to bring LLVM to production quality.
Began developing the Swift programming language at Apple; also received ACM SIGPLAN Programming Languages Software Award for LLVM.
Apple publicly launched Swift at WWDC, making it a primary language for iOS/macOS development.
Left Apple; briefly VP Autopilot Software at Tesla, then joined Google on TensorFlow infrastructure and co-founded MLIR.
Co-founded Modular AI to build Mojo and an AI developer platform after SiFive platform engineering role.

name: Allison Parrish
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found in reviewed sources (Wikipedia: year of birth missing). Notable work includes @everyword Twitter bot (2007–2014) and later academic roles at NYU ITP, but age at those milestones cannot be verified.
early_history_summary: Poet, programmer, and game designer from Bountiful, Utah. BA Linguistics UC Berkeley; MPS Interactive Telecommunications Program, NYU. Known for literary Twitter bots and computational poetry; Assistant Arts Professor at NYU ITP since 2016.
evidence_summary: Creative coding reputation is clear by the mid-2010s (Village Voice 'Best Maker of Poetry Bots' 2016), but without a birth year eligibility by age 26 cannot be coded.

name: Frederick Lenz
milestone_by_age_26: Born February 9, 1950. By age 26 he was an advanced English literature student / early spiritual teacher under Sri Chinmoy, not a software founder. Documented software companies (AutoSys and others) and business success came in the 1980s–1990s when he was in his 30s–40s; no material tech milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born San Diego; family moved to Stamford, Connecticut. Earned MA and Ph.D. in English Literature at SUNY Stony Brook; began studying with Sri Chinmoy in 1972 and teaching meditation by his late 20s. Later known as Rama/Zen Master Rama; software design activity with student-founded companies occurred in the 1980s–90s.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources beyond early move from California to Connecticut.
evidence_summary: Listed under American software engineers due to later software design/advisor roles, but primary notability is spiritual teaching and writing. Tech entrepreneurship milestones are post-26. Died 1998 at age 48.

name: Christoph Bregler
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found. Diplom Karlsruhe 1993 and M.S./Ph.D. UC Berkeley (1995/1998) are documented, but without birth year age at those degrees cannot be verified for ≤26 eligibility.
early_history_summary: Computer vision researcher; Diplom University of Karlsruhe (1993), M.S. and Ph.D. UC Berkeley (1995, 1998). Later faculty at Stanford and NYU; CEO ManhattanMocap; Senior Director/Distinguished Scientist at Google DeepMind working on media integrity and deepfakes.
evidence_summary: Strong academic/industry trajectory, but Ph.D. in 1998 is the early academic peak and birth year is unavailable, so age-26 eligibility cannot be established.

name: Sylvain Gugger
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found. Self-described path: math Master's, brief Ph.D. attempt, then ~7 years teaching undergrads in Paris before discovering deep learning via fast.ai MOOC in late 2017—clearly a mid-career pivot, not an age-≤26 breakout.
early_history_summary: French mathematician/teacher who entered deep learning after a NYT article and fast.ai course (2017–2018), then became core fast.ai contributor and co-author, later Research Engineer at Hugging Face (Transformers), and subsequently ML engineer at Jane Street.
family_context_summary: Mentions father introducing him to BASIC at age 13; otherwise not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father encouraged early programming exposure (BASIC); not a professional domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Public 2019 fast.ai essay documents multi-year teaching career before ML. Major open-source impact (fastai, HF Transformers) occurred after that pivot; no verified ≤26 material milestone.

name: Sean Egan
milestone_by_age_26: Became maintainer of Gaim/Pidgin (major multi-protocol open-source IM client) in early 2002 at age ~19–20 after contributing since 2000; hired by Google onto Google Talk in September 2005 at age 23 and published a technical book on Gaim development the same year.
early_history_summary: Born April 5, 1982, on Long Island, New York; Chaminade High School and B.S. computer science at Binghamton University. Began contributing to Gaim in 2000 (age 18), joined the official team January 2001, and led the project from early 2002 until 2008 while it was a leading free multi-protocol messenger.
primary_early_advantage_tags: open-source community, early IM client reps, Google Talk hire
evidence_summary: Wikipedia biography and Pidgin developer page confirm birth date April 5, 1982 and maintainer role from early 2002. Forbes (2002) discusses Gaim and Egan as a developer during the AOL conflict era; CNET/Wikinews covered Google hiring the Gaim lead. Family background not documented; success tier 4 as specialist notable rather than global icon.
starting_point: Born on Long Island, New York; educated at Chaminade High School and Binghamton University in computer science. Family class/background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Software engineer associated with Google (historically Google Talk/libjingle; Wikipedia notes Google Maps work); former long-time Pidgin/Gaim project lead.

trajectory.event: Began contributing to the open-source multi-protocol IM client Gaim (later Pidgin).
Became an official member of the Gaim/Pidgin development team.
Became project maintainer of Gaim/Pidgin, a leading free multi-protocol instant messaging client.
Hired by Google as a software engineer on Google Talk; published 'Open Source Messaging Application Development: Building and Extending Gaim'.
Announced retirement as Pidgin maintainer after leading the project for about six years.

name: Eric Schiermeyer
milestone_by_age_26: UK Companies House lists DOB January 1978. Best-documented material milestone is co-founding Zynga in April 2007 at age ~29. Earlier eUniverse/Intermix CTO claims (circa 1999–2000s) are weakly dual-dated in high-quality independent sources relative to age 26, so no clearly verified material ≤26 milestone coded.
early_history_summary: Attended UC Santa Cruz (BA Philosophy, reported 1993–97). Worked in early internet content/social (eUniverse/Intermix/MySpace-era roles per secondary profiles), co-founded Zynga in 2007 with Mark Pincus et al., later founded Luminary and Gala Games (blockchain gaming).
evidence_summary: Zynga co-founding is solid (Wikipedia Zynga founders list) but at ~age 29. Birth month/year from UK company filings; early CTO timelines are secondary/profile sites without strong contemporaneous dual confirmation for a ≤26 material event.
